clue.text: Looked good, area outside church

indicators.note: the area word sits outside, wrapping round the church letters

parts.note: an area of territory is land
CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone looked handsome, standing in the grounds around a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To have glanced is to have taken a quick look, so the past tense matches the past-tense clue verb.

clue.text: Musical riff — it continues along the entire record

definitions.meaning: a rhythmic feel or pattern in jazz and funk

definitions.text: it continues along the entire record
definitions.meaning: a vinyl disc has one spiral channel cut from the edge to the centre

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an infectious rhythm and the single spiral channel that the stylus follows on vinyl.

clue.text: Directed cast, or …?

indicators.note: directed suggests the letters are put through new moves, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A theatre director wonders what else to call the cast.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the cast of a play, directed, are its players.
explanation.definitionFit: The cast of a play is the company of performers, the people who play its parts.

clue.text: Measure bit in middle

indicators.note: the bit word goes inside the middle word

parts.note: the middle is the centre
a bit can mean a while or a spell of time

explanation.surface: Measuring out a small piece in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit' looks like a small piece but means a period, as in 'wait a bit'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a unit of length in the metric system, one hundredth of a metre.

clue.text: Wisdom of department opening in hospital

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word hospital is taken

explanation.surface: Insight from a department newly opened in a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Depth of thought means profundity or intellectual insight, the deep understanding that wisdom implies.

clue.text: It could be blooming useless, initially, if cash is wasted

indicators.note: wasted means ruined or thrown about, so these letters are scrambled
only the opening letter of the word useless is taken

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grumble that a garden plant is a blooming waste of money if cash is squandered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' looks like a mild British expletive, but it is the definition's flowering sense. U, IF and CASH are mixed by 'wasted'; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This shrub is grown for its hanging purple and red flowers, so it is an example of something in bloom.

clue.text: Concerned with how the bread gets sliced?

definitions.text: Concerned with how the bread gets sliced?

parts.words: Concerned with how the bread gets sliced?
parts.note: bread is slang for money, so how it is divided up is a monetary matter

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a baker or a sandwich; bread is slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything to do with money, its division and management, is a monetary or fiscal matter.

clue.text: Pretty cold pick-up truck

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
ute is Australian slang for a utility vehicle or pick-up

explanation.surface: Describing a rather cold pick-up truck.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty and appealing in an endearing way is a synonym of attractive or sweet.

clue.text: Stop before one gets on horse

indicators.note: the stopping word comes before the remaining pieces

parts.note: to stall is to stop or come to a halt
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone halts before one of them climbs on the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an uncastrated adult male horse kept for breeding.

clue.text: Gemstone set my hat off

indicators.note: off means wrong or awry, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone takes a jewel-studded hat off.
explanation.definitionFit: This purple variety of quartz is a precious stone used in jewellery.

clue.text: Temper — losing head on a regular basis

indicators.note: the first letter of the synonym is dropped, as a head is the top of a word

parts.note: to temper something is to soften or moderate it

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper on a regular basis.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something frequently means doing it repeatedly, on a regular footing.

clue.text: Enter a tent and peer around

indicators.note: around signals the letters are turned about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to go into a tent and have a look about.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce or get into something is to enter it; both verbs mean going inside.

clue.text: Queen, in leaving, is putting a coat on?

indicators.note: the queen's letter goes inside the word for leaving

parts.note: something vanishing is disappearing or leaving
R is short for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A queen putting her coat on as she goes out.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures someone dressing to depart; the definition is applying a coat of varnish. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying varnish means brushing a protective layer of gloss over wood, which is literally coating it.

clue.text: Starts to believe Liberal's acting honourably? Nonsense!

indicators.note: the starting letter of each of the following four words is taken

explanation.surface: Scepticism at the idea that a Liberal politician might behave honourably.
explanation.definitionFit: Blah is dismissive slang for empty talk or rubbish, an exclamation like 'rubbish!'.

clue.text: Celebrity goes on vacation, but not Central America — result of lack of fare?

indicators.note: the second piece goes on after the celebrity word

parts.note: a celebrity is a star

indicators.note: the letters of Central America are taken out of the word vacation

parts.note: CA is the abbreviation for Central America

explanation.surface: A star goes on holiday but avoids Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fare' is food here, not a ticket price, which the holiday surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of food leads to extreme hunger and suffering, the condition of going without nourishment.

clue.text: Sketches depict sins or misbehaving

indicators.note: misbehaving letters are out of line, so they get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Drawings that portray wrongdoing or naughty behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sketches can be brief accounts or portrayals in words, which is what descriptions are.

clue.text: Youth clubs kept secret about large violent criminal

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

indicators.note: the kept-secret word goes about the large letter

parts.note: to have kept something secret is to have hid it
hood is slang for a hoodlum, a violent criminal

explanation.surface: Young people in youth clubs hiding a big thug.
explanation.definitionFit: Youth is the early period of life, the years before adulthood.

clue.text: Small bed detached without injury

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
something detached is loose or free

explanation.surface: A small bed that has come apart without anyone being hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: To get away unharmed or unpunished is the idiom of escaping without penalty.

clue.text: Throttle — unusual to be squeezed by learner? On the contrary

indicators.note: one piece is pressed inside the other
the reverse of what the words say: the learner is squeezed by the unusual word

parts.note: something unusual is strange
L is the learner plate symbol

explanation.surface: An odd learner driver is being throttled.
explanation.definitionFit: To throttle someone is to choke them by the throat, the same violent act.

clue.text: They make tracks for these garden bugs

definitions.meaning: Caterpillar tracks are the continuous linked treads on tanks and bulldozers
the larvae of butterflies and moths that chew garden leaves

explanation.walkthrough: 'for these' links the two senses: the tread on heavy vehicles and the leaf-eating larvae.
explanation.definitionFit: The trademark tread belt on tractors shares its name with the crawling larvae of moths and butterflies.

clue.text: Rubbish issue

definitions.meaning: a brood of offspring born to an animal at one time

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both scattered refuse and a group of young animals born together, like puppies.

clue.text: Grass's condition after batting

indicators.note: the condition word comes after the batting word

parts.note: in cricket, the side batting is said to be in
form means fitness or condition, as in good form

explanation.surface: A grass pitch is in good condition after the batsmen have been in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' is the slang verb meaning to tell on someone, not the lawn the cricket surface suggests. 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To grass is British slang for snitching, giving police information on someone.

clue.text: Attempt to hold a platter

indicators.note: the attempt word holds the A inside it

parts.note: an attempt is a try

explanation.surface: Someone trying to keep a serving dish steady.
explanation.definitionFit: A platter is a large flat serving plate, much like a flat carrier for food and drinks.

clue.text: Regard maid oddly getting dismissed — I'm flipping helping!

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the word maid are thrown out, leaving the even ones
flipping turns the letters of I'm over, back to front

parts.note: I'm gives the letters I and M
a helping is a portion or ration of food

explanation.surface: Someone sacks a maid for strange behaviour and then insists they are helping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regard' is a noun here, as in high esteem. 'oddly getting dismissed' leaves AD from maid; 'flipping' turns I'm into MI.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold someone in high regard is to feel respect and esteem for them.

clue.text: Hopeless in record time

parts.note: taken as written
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A despairing note about something in record time.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hopeless at something means being clumsy, incompetent and without skill.

clue.text: All the best volunteers will show up twice

indicators.note: the volunteer letters appear two times over

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A farewell as volunteers turn up twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will show up' is a link, meaning the letters simply appear. TA is the Territorial Army, the UK's part-time reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A British informal goodbye, like saying cheerio or so long.

clue.text: Doctor with duty to follow mother's rambling discourse

indicators.note: the duty word follows the mother word in the answer

parts.note: to doctor something is to tamper with or rig it
ma is an informal word for mother
a duty or function is a role

explanation.surface: A doctor whose duty is to sit through his mother's long, wandering talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a medic but is the verb meaning falsify. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-winded, confused account or procedure is a meandering speech that goes on and on.

clue.text: Start to strain?

parts.note: a strain is a tune, and the opening bars that lead into a tune come before its melody proper

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the effort of pushing or sieving; here strain is a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: The short opening passage of a song leads into the melody, which old-fashioned language calls a strain.

clue.text: Green or red male's pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are a bad mess to be reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether a man's trousers are green or red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like trousers, but in British slang it means poor or rubbish, signalling the anagram. 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This shade is a bright gem-like green, named after the green precious stone.

clue.text: Paddy Brown's first to take drink

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word take is used

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: An Irishman called Brown is the first to have a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' looks like an Irish name but is British slang for a fit of temper. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a paddy is a fit of rage, an outburst like a child's sulk.
